trajectory_summary: The call opens on a hard objection — customer states the decision is already made — and the rep uses the schema's signed-with-someone comparison strategy to convert a dead-sounding call into a booked in-person visit within about three minutes. But the win is thin: the rep never probes which company the son signed with, what the terms were, or what the design looked like, so the closer walks in blind on the competitive intelligence that would make the apples-to-apples pitch work. The son — who holds the utility account and independently made the competitor decision — is not looped into the new appointment at all, leaving the booking structurally fragile despite the smooth booking mechanics.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag unknown; observed outcome is a booked in-person appointment for Saturday the 22nd at 12PM, but it should be flagged as conditional/fragile rather than a clean win — the actual decision-maker (the son, who has utility in his name and already picked a competitor) is explicitly not going to be present.
